newsitem.title: UK: EMS/Mark recovers in Europe as dollar falters.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark recovers in Europe as dollar falters.

text.p: The mark recovered from earlier lows on its European crosses on Friday, boosted by a sharp fall in the dollar.
Dealers cited nervousness ahead of the Bundesbank repo tender on Tuesday and council meeting on Thursday as well as thin, technically-dominated trade as reasons for the late shake-up.
"The mark/crosses is taking its cue from the dollar/mark slide," said a trader at a UK bank.
Dollar/mark slumped in U.S dealings, falling to a low of 1.8155 marks. U.S. asset markets also weakened sharply.
The Dow Industrials tumbled over 100 points and Germany's IBIS Dax index was also weaker, dipping below 4,100 points in afternoon dealings.
Traders said with much of Europe away on holiday, movements in the mark crosses had been exacerbated due to thin volumes.
